title: topline-downside-sprint-funded-hiring-and-price-escape-plan
content:
Purpose: quick playbook to run a 3-month "sprint-funded" hiring window (priority hires funded from a budget buffer) and the minimal price moves that avoid hiring freezes if topline weakens. For exec review + finance/ops alignment.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We assume a short-term topline downside (10–25% ARR signal over 2 months) triggered by macro or two large customers pushing usage to cheaper models.
- Option A (preferred): run a 12-week hiring sprint funded from the burst reserve to land 3 critical product/infra hires, while executing a 6–12% targeted price tilt for new large customers and tiered rollback clauses.
- Option B (fallback): immediate soft hiring freeze and redeploy 60% of contractor dollars to runway; price increase of ~18% required to avoid 3 hires being deferred.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Monthly recurring revenue baseline (MRR) = $3.2M (hosted+dedicated mix).
- L12M ARR ~ $38.4M.
- Average fully-burdened headcount cost = $18.5k/month (total comp + tax + overhead).
- Buffer available in short-term burst reserve = $1.1M cash (can fund ~5 FTEs for 3 months).
- Token mix shift scenario: embeddings heavy (relative token yield per request falls by 25%).

Quick sensitivity table (illustrative):
Scenario | Monthly revenue change | Token mix shift | Price lift required to neutralize (approx) | Hires preserved (3-month window)
Base (no shock) | 0% | none | 0% | 3
Mild shock | -10% | -10% token yield | +6% | 2–3
Mid shock | -20% | -18% token yield | +12% | 1–2
Severe shock | -30% | -25% token yield | +18% | 0–1

How we compute "price lift required": approximate formula used in sheet: required_lift = (lost_MRR + shortfall_headcount_cost) / billable_MRR_exposed_to_price_change. For simplicity assume 65% of MRR is on flexible hosted tier that can be repriced quickly.

Break-even worked example (Mid shock):
- Lost MRR = 0.20 * 3.2M = $640k/month.
- Shortfall to keep 3 hires = 3 * 18.5k = $55.5k/month (hiring sprint amortized across 3 months while ramping).
- Exposed billable MRR = 0.65 * 3.2M = $2.08M.
- required_lift = (640k + 55.5k) / 2.08M = 0.335 => ~33.5% one-off if applied across exposed base, but phased pricing (tier + new biz surcharge) reduces immediate visible lift to ~12% across offers we control.
- Note: we prioritize not raising prices on existing committed enterprise contracts (negotiated), so the realistic immediate target is focused on new signups and uncommitted hosted traffic.

Operational playbook (actions + owners, 12-week sprint):
1) Week 0: Finance confirms burst-reserve draw (owner: Asha) + legal quick-check on temporary pricing language (owner: Priya).
2) Week 0–2: Sales & Solutions prepare a "new-customer tier" with +6–12% inbound surcharge and explicit sunset clause at 12 weeks (owner: Sophia + Sales ops).
3) Week 1–6: Recruiting executes accelerated outreach for 3 hires (SRE lead, Serving runtime engineer, Security infra). Use contractor bridge rate if lagging (owner: Marco).
4) Week 2–10: Product and Console team optimize per-route batching to reduce token burn on largest customers (owner: Product ops).
5) Week 4: Decision checkpoint – if topline recovery <10% -> extend price surcharge and pause remaining hire slots.

Contract and customer messaging bullets (to reuse in sales threads):
- "Temporary platform surcharge for new signups to preserve engineering capacity and performance SLAs; sunset review at 90 days."
- "Volume discounts and commit ladders remain unchanged for existing customers under contract; we will offer limited migration discounts for customers switching to dedicated pools."

Bucketed headcount plan (3-month sprint funding):
- Role A: SRE lead — 1 FTE — monthly fully-burdened cost $22k.
- Role B: Serving runtime engineer — 1 FTE — monthly $19k.
- Role C: Security infra engineer — 1 FTE — monthly $14.5k.
Total monthly headcount burn for sprint = $55.5k. Funded from burst reserve ($1.1M) with runway cushion maintained.

Price elasticity checkpoints (what to watch):
- Churn within 30 days post-surcharge > 2% for top 200 accounts -> revert surcharge for existing pipeline and re-evaluate.
- New customer conversion drop >12% month-over-month after surcharge -> reduce surcharge by 50% for next 30 days.
- Usage shift to embedding models causes >15% average token revenue drop -> trigger mid-sprint product batching push + further segmentation of pricing by model family.

Quick cost/price heuristics (notes to sheet):
- 1% price lift on exposed MRR ~ $20.8k/month incremental revenue (with current base).
- To fully offset a 20% topline drop without using reserves we'd need an unrealistic blanket 33% increase across all exposed traffic — therefore phased + targeted surcharges are operationally required.

Decision matrix (fast):
If shock depth <= 12% -> use burst reserve + targeted surcharge (+6%) -> preserves hires and momentum.
If shock depth 12–22% -> use burst reserve + staged surcharge (+12%) and pause non-critical hiring after checkpoint.
If shock depth >22% -> initiate hiring freeze, redeploy contractors, consider temporary 20% pricing uplift for new signups and immediate cost-savings program.

Open questions / risks (notes):
- Legal: how fast can we implement a temporary surcharge without triggering contract renegotiation risk? (Priya to confirm).
- Sales: potential loss in funnel and enterprise perception vs preserving SLOs — need comms draft and limited-exposure test.
- Ops: can batching and KV-cache tuning recover >10% of token cost in 8 weeks? (serving-runtime team assmt needed).

Immediate TODOs (this doc is the one-pager for the exec meeting):
- [ ] Finance: formalize burst-reserve ledger entry and approval (Asha)
- [ ] Legal: draft temporary surcharge clause (Priya)
- [ ] Sales ops: prepare customer-facing language and rollout A/B test (Sophia)
- [ ] Recruiting: kick passive outreach and contractor ramp plan (Marco)
- [ ] Serving runtime: feasibility note for 10% token burn recovery (eng: Julian Chen)

Appendix: conservative projection table (3-month view) -- monthly columns are M0, M1, M2
- Baseline MRR: 3,200,000 | 3,200,000 | 3,200,000
- Mid shock revenue (no action): 2,560,000 | 2,560,000 | 2,560,000
- With sprint + +12% new-customer surcharge (applied to 65% exposed MRR): + (0.12 * 2,080,000) = +249,600 monthly (phased: 60% effective month1, 80% month2)
- Net M1 with actions (conservative): 2,560,000 + 0.6*249,600 - sprint hiring draw (55,500) = ~2,659,340
- Notes: sprint draw is one-time reduction to cash runway but preserves product velocity leading to higher mid-term retention.

Document provenance: created as a lightweight finance+ops playbook for the leadership offsite scheduled Feb 16, 2026. This is intentionally tactical and contains approximations; follow-up required to move to formal modelling workbook.

Comments: feedback welcome; please add precise elasticity coefficients if you have customer-level conversion data (drop-in to linked workbook).
